STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: The core ETag logic held up under every probe I could build: hashing, weak If-None-Match parsing, 304 handling, HEAD, Flush/Hijack/Unwrap, panics, 1xx, and Compress/Recoverer composition. One reproduced divergence from net/http: headers set after the first write are applied to the wire, so a buggy handler gets a broken response. Two minor items and a documented caveat round it out.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probes were `middleware/zz_probe_*_test.go`, all deleted; `git status` is unchanged: M README.md, A middleware/etag.go, A middleware/etag_test.go)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Headers set after the first Write leak onto the wire. Probe: handler does `Write("hello")`, then `Header().Set("Content-Length","1000")`. Native net/http gives `Content-Length: 5` and a clean 200. Wrapped gives `Content-Length: 1000` and the client fails with `readErr=unexpected EOF`. The buffering moves the header snapshot to after the handler returns, so late header mutations now take effect. Fix: snapshot the headers at the first Write/WriteHeader (e.g. clone `w.Header()` into a stored header map and apply it at finish) or document and test it.
- [minor] `WriteHeader(0)` is accepted silently: the wrapper yields 200, while net/http panics with "invalid WriteHeader code 0". Reproduced: `status=200`, no panic.
- [minor] `Compress(ETag(h))` gives gzip and identity responses the same ETag. Reproduced: identity request carrying the gzip ETag gets `304`. The doc comment warns about this ordering, so it is a caveat, not a doc mismatch. Consider a test pinning the recommended order.
- [minor] Test gaps: no test for handler-set malformed `abc` ETag, handler-written `WriteHeader(304)`, `ResponseController` Flush/SetWriteDeadline, or Compress composition. All of these behave correctly in my probes.
- [minor] Not reproduced: the wrapper drops `ReadFrom`, so `io.Copy` loses sendfile. Performance only.

CHECKS:
- Method cases: POST/PUT/"get" with matching If-None-Match -> pass (200, no ETag added).
- Computed ETag: single, chunked, explicit 200, empty body, and a 3 MB body written in 1000-byte chunks -> pass (bytes identical).
- Handler-set `W/"x"` kept -> pass.
- HEAD: no-body gets no ETag; body-HEAD ETag equals GET ETag; HEAD with `*` -> 304 -> pass. Content-Length deleted on HEAD 304 -> pass.
- If-None-Match corpus (comma-in-quote, malformed members, case, prefix, weak, `*`, multi-line, OWS) -> pass (in existing tests; re-checked with `"abc"` vs handler `abc` -> 200).
- Handler-set `abc` ETag with If-None-Match `"abc"` -> 200 (no match); with `*` -> 304 -> pass.
- Handler `WriteHeader(304)` with If-None-Match -> 304 passthrough, ETag kept -> pass.
- Non-200 passthrough, ServeContent Range -> 206 with no ETag, bad range -> 416 -> pass.
- Flush/RC: `ResponseController.Flush` and `SetWriteDeadline` inside handler -> pass.
- Hijack after buffered write -> identical raw bytes to native -> pass.
- Recoverer outer on panic (after write, and with handler ETag) -> 500, empty body -> pass.
- Recoverer inner -> 200 "x" with ETag, same as native -> pass.
- Wire parity GET/HEAD at 0/5/1500/2100/5000 bytes (Content-Length vs chunked, Content-Type sniff, trailers) -> pass.
- README row: column width 100 matches neighbors; link line placed alphabetically -> pass.
- Not run here (orchestrator did): `go test -race ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt`.

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should late header mutation be made native-identical (snapshot headers at first write), or accepted as a documented difference? The first option is the one I'd choose; it is a small fix in `etag.go`.
